exposure: antenatal diagnosis of fetal orofacial cleft (OFC)
presence of other structural abnormalities (syndromic vs. non-syndromic)
type of prenatal diagnostic testing (conventional karyotyping vs. chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA))
cohort: Pregnant women (N=66) with an antenatal diagnosis of fetal orofacial cleft (OFC) between January 2016 and December 2020.
finding: Invasive prenatal tests with Chromosomal Microarray Analysis (CMA) provided an incremental diagnostic yield over conventional karyotyping for fetuses with OFC, and a negative result for genomic variants in non-syndromic OFC cases was significantly associated with good long-term outcomes.
